parentQuestion: Our employee is covered by the Employment Act and the overtime provisions. Do ordinary salary and overtime have the same payment deadline after the salary period ends? Explain the practical payroll steps and cite the relevant official guidance. No journal is required.
assistantAnswer:
# Answer

Ordinary salary and overtime do not have the same payment deadline after the salary period ends under the Employment Act guidelines. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Under Ministry of Manpower official guidance, ordinary salary must be paid within 7 days after the end of the salary period. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Under Ministry of Manpower official guidance, payment for overtime work must be made within 14 days after the end of the salary period. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Employers must issue itemised pay slips to employees covered by the Employment Act. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Employers must keep detailed employment records, including salary records, of employees covered by the Employment Act. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Payment can be made directly into the employee's bank account or by cheque, where the cheque needs to be cleared by the bank before the employee is considered paid. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)
